attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The missing estimate is the mixed reflected Wilson collar trace: uniformly control \(S_{a,L}(\Theta W_{R,a}(C_i^\delta)W_{R,a}(C_j^\delta))\) as \(a\downarrow0\) and \(\delta\downarrow0\), proving that no cusp, intersection, hairpin, or reflection-plane counterterm appears in any OS matrix entry.
steps: Fix a finite list \(F_1,\ldots,F_N\) in the gauge-invariant positive-time core and coefficients \(c_i\). For each \(\delta>0\), replace \(F_i\) by \(T_\delta F_i\), so every reflected product is separated from the reflection plane.

By regulated reflection positivity, \(Q_{a,L}(T_\delta F,c)\ge0\) for every cutoff. By the RG-to-OS convergence assumption for fixed collars, pass to the cutoff limit to obtain \(Q_S(T_\delta F,c)\ge0\). This part is a valid closed-cone argument and contains no new Yang-Mills singular analysis.

To remove the collar, try to write \(Q_S(F,c)=\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}Q_S(T_\delta F,c)\). For local mirror-flat composites, expand into finitely many Schwinger distributions and use \(T_\delta f\to f\); this gives the trace limit.

For Wilson-loop generators, the same expansion is unavailable because \(\Theta W(C_i^\delta)W(C_j^\delta)\) can create a boundary contact in the reflected pair. The trace limit therefore requires a mixed, pairwise no-boundary-renormalization estimate, not just continuity of individual loop expectations.
If the mixed trace modulus holds, then \(Q_S(F,c)\) is a limit of nonnegative numbers and hence nonnegative. OS-density of the core then extends positivity to the intended \(\mathcal A_+\).

If a residual boundary factor \(B_a^{ij}\ne1\) appears, the derivation proves at most positivity for a different algebra with an inserted boundary renormalization; that violates the same-theory condition.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The fixed-collar positivity transfer is valid, but the current assumptions do not yet rule out a boundary anomaly in Wilson-loop pairings. Without that estimate, the limit \(Q_S(T_\delta F,c)\to Q_S(F,c)\) is exactly the point at issue, so full OS positivity for the same continuum Yang-Mills observables has not been proved.

assumptions: For every cutoff \((a,L)\), \(S_{a,L}\) is reflection-positive on \(\mathcal A_{a,+}\): all finite OS matrices \(S_{a,L}(\Theta I_aF_i,I_aF_j)\) are positive semidefinite.

For each fixed \(\delta>0\), the RG/cutoff-removal topology is strong enough to give convergence of every finite collar-separated reflected quadratic form \(Q_{a,L}(T_\delta F,c)\to Q_S(T_\delta F,c)\).

The collar maps are internal to the locked same-theory algebra: \(T_\delta F\in\mathcal A_+\), \(T_\delta F\to F\), and \(I_aT_\delta F\) is the regulated representative of the same observable, not a separately renormalized boundary observable.

Mixed Wilson trace modulus: for each finite list \(F_i\) in a dense core generated by local mirror-flat composites and mirror-smooth Wilson loops, \(Q_S(T_\delta F,c)\to Q_S(F,c)\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\), uniformly enough to interchange the cutoff limit and the collar limit.

No-new-boundary-renormalization: in every reflected pair \(\Theta C_i^\delta\cup C_j^\delta\), the renormalization needed as \(\delta\downarrow0\) is exactly the same multiplicative/local renormalization already assigned to the individual continuum observables; any residual boundary contact factor must tend to one.
The dense core is OS-dense: every intended positive-time gauge-invariant observable is approximable in the seminorm \(\|F\|_{OS}^2=Q_S(F,1)\) by finite combinations from the core.
definitions: source object: a cutoff net \(S_{a,L}\) of reflection-positive Euclidean Yang-Mills Schwinger functionals on a fixed gauge-invariant positive-time observable algebra \(\mathcal A_{a,+}\), including local mirror-flat composites and renormalized Wilson observables \(W_{R,a}(C)\).

target object: a continuum Schwinger functional \(S\) on a gauge-invariant positive-time algebra \(\mathcal A_+\) whose finite reflected quadratic forms define an OS-positive pre-Hilbert space after quotienting null vectors.

controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions, controlled by convergence of finite collar-separated reflected quadratic forms plus a boundary trace modulus as the collar width tends to zero.

same-theory condition: the embeddings \(I_a:\mathcal A_+\to\mathcal A_{a,+}\) and collar maps \(T_\delta:\mathcal A_+\to\mathcal A_+\) use the same renormalized Wilson/local observables before and after the limit; no extra reflection-plane counterterm, cusp factor, boundary field, or algebra enlargement is allowed.

\(T_\delta\) denotes a positive-time collaring/smoothing operation moving all supports or contours into \(t\ge \delta\), preserving gauge invariance and converging to the identity in the intended continuum observable topology.

A mixed reflected Wilson pairing means an insertion of the form \(S(\Theta W_R(C_i)\,W_R(C_j))\), or a finite linear combination of such insertions, because OS positivity tests the product of a reflected observable with an unreflected one.

equations.label: regulated positivity
equations.valid_when: Valid for finite lists \(F_i\in\mathcal A_+\) whose regulated representatives lie in the positive-time lattice/gauge-invariant algebra on which reflection positivity is established.

equations.label: fixed-collar closed-cone transfer
equations.valid_when: Valid when the cutoff-removal topology controls each finite reflected quadratic form with supports separated from the reflection plane by the collar \(\delta\).

equations.label: mixed trace modulus
equations.valid_when: Valid only if all mixed reflected insertions \(S(\Theta T_\delta F_i,T_\delta F_j)\) have boundary values at \(t=0\) in the same observable algebra.

equations.label: no boundary anomaly diagnostic
equations.latex: \lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\limsup_{a\downarrow0}\left|B_a^{ij}(\delta)-1\right|=0,\quad B_a^{ij}(\delta):=\frac{\text{renormalization of }\Theta C_i^\delta\cup C_j^\delta}{\text{product of the prescribed renormalizations of }C_i^\delta\text{ and }C_j^\delta}
equations.valid_when: Valid as a same-theory test for Wilson-loop sectors; a nontrivial limit of \(B_a^{ij}\) is a falsifier of the bridge even if positivity could be restored in a modified boundary algebra.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Construct a mirror-smooth or hairpin Wilson-loop family for which \(B_a^{ij}(\delta)\) has a non-unit limit or behaves like a cusp/contact anomalous factor. Such an example is a falsifier of the same-theory condition and blocks the bridge.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma would complete the non-tautological part of the OS positivity passage: closedness gives positivity for fixed collars, while the mixed trace modulus carries positivity to observables touching the reflection plane without changing the theory.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Mixed Wilson-collar trace bridge: assume regulated gauge-invariant Schwinger functionals are reflection-positive, converge on all fixed positive-time collars, and satisfy a no-new-boundary-renormalization trace modulus for every finite reflected Wilson pairing. Then the continuum Schwinger functional is OS-positive on the OS-closure of the same gauge-invariant algebra. The essential sharpening is that the trace modulus must be mixed in the OS quadratic form, not merely pointwise for single Wilson loops.

assumptions: The continuum local-composite Schwinger functions are distributions on the chosen test-function space.
The collar maps act by smooth translations/cutoffs on smearing functions and preserve mirror-flatness.
Composite renormalization has already been fixed in the bulk and does not introduce a separate boundary counterterm for mirror-flat smearing.
definitions: Local mirror-flat core: finite products of renormalized gauge-invariant local composites \(\mathcal O_k(x)\), smeared by \(f_k\in C_c^\infty(t\ge0)\) whose jets at \(t=0\) match the reflected smoothness required by \(\Theta\).
Distributional trace condition: \(T_\delta f\to f\) in the test-function topology in which the continuum Schwinger distribution \(S_n\) is continuous.
OS seminorm continuity: \(F_n\to F\) in the core topology implies \(Q_S(F_n-F,c)\to0\) for every fixed finite coefficient vector \(c\).

equations.label: distributional collar convergence
equations.valid_when: Valid for local composite insertions if \(T_\delta f_k\to f_k\) in the nuclear test-function topology dual to the Schwinger distributions.

equations.label: local OS trace
equations.valid_when: Valid for finite lists from the local mirror-flat core after expanding the quadratic form into finitely many distributional pairings.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A required boundary counterterm for mirror-flat local smearings would contradict the assumed bulk-only composite renormalization and would be a falsifier for using the local core as a same-theory dense domain.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This sublemma separates a tractable local-field boundary-value argument from the genuinely Wilson-loop/nonlocal obstruction.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For gauge-invariant local composite fields smeared by test functions that are smooth and flat to sufficient order at the reflection plane, the collar trace modulus follows from ordinary distributional continuity of the continuum Schwinger distributions, so this sector is not the main obstruction.

assumptions: Wilson-loop renormalization distinguishes smooth contour divergences from cusp/intersection divergences.
The limiting reflected contour is allowed by the intended test algebra, so excluding it would shrink the theory rather than prove positivity for it.
The anomalous factor contributes to at least one finite OS quadratic form and cannot be absorbed into a null vector quotient.
definitions: Hairpin family: a family of positive-time contours \(C_\delta\) whose reflected product \(\Theta C_\delta\cup C_\delta\) has a limiting tangent discontinuity or self-contact at \(t=0\).
Boundary anomaly factor: a residual multiplicative or additive renormalization in the mixed reflected expectation that is not generated by the prescribed bulk Wilson-loop renormalizations.
Same-theory obstruction: any non-unit boundary anomaly factor changes the observable identification across cutoff removal, even if the modified OS matrix is positive.

equations.label: cusp anomaly pattern
equations.valid_when: Valid as the expected obstruction pattern when the collar collapse creates an angle \(\theta\) with nonzero cusp anomalous dimension.

equations.label: failed same-theory trace
equations.valid_when: Valid as a falsifier when the left side exists only after an extra boundary/cusp renormalization not present in the prescribed continuum observable.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find one finite OS matrix whose entries require a non-unit \(B_a^{ij}\); then the same-theory bridge lemma is false for that algebra.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This is the negative bridge lemma: it turns a vague concern about Wilson loops into a concrete test that can kill the same-theory OS passage.
candidate_lemmas.statement: If a sequence of reflected Wilson collar pairings develops a nontrivial cusp, intersection, or hairpin anomalous factor at the reflection plane, then the closed-cone positivity argument may remain valid for a modified renormalized algebra but fails to prove OS positivity for the original same Yang-Mills theory.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot away from this branch if a hairpin/cusp reflected Wilson family yields a non-unit boundary anomaly factor that cannot be removed without changing the test algebra.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if one proves an angle-uniform mixed Wilson collar estimate \(B_a^{ij}(\delta)\to1\) for a dense mirror-smooth Wilson/local core and establishes OS-density in the resulting seminorm.
control_decision.reason: The branch is still producing nontrivial refinements: the bottleneck has narrowed from generic trace continuity to mixed reflected Wilson trace continuity, giving a concrete valid proof target and a concrete falsifier pattern.

dependency_updates.description: Split into a formal fixed-collar closed-cone step and a non-formal boundary trace step. The formal step is valid under convergence of finite reflected collar forms; the remaining bridge is the mixed Wilson trace modulus.

The algebra must be locked before the limit and must include a core where collaring is internal. For Wilson loops, same-theory means no extra boundary/cusp normalization in reflected pairings, not merely well-defined individual loop expectations.

The topology must dominate finite OS quadratic forms for collar-separated probes and must be compatible with the \(\delta\downarrow0\) boundary value. Individual Schwinger convergence is insufficient unless it implies convergence of mixed reflected matrices.

falsifiers: A concrete hairpin Wilson-loop family whose reflected product has \(B_a^{ij}(\delta)\to B\ne1\) or a cusp anomalous divergence is a decisive falsifier of the same-theory bridge.

The cutoff-removal topology controls individual Wilson-loop expectations but not mixed reflected expectations \(S(\Theta W(C_i)W(C_j))\); then closed-cone transfer is too weak to be valid for OS positivity.

The collar map \(T_\delta\) changes the Wilson-loop renormalization scheme, for example by replacing a boundary-touching contour with a separately normalized smooth contour; positivity would then be proved for a different test algebra.

Reflection positivity holds only for bare lattice Wilson observables, while the renormalized Wilson observables needed in the continuum require subtractions or counterterms that are not reflection-positive.
OS-density fails: local mirror-flat composites and mirror-smooth Wilson collars do not approximate the intended gauge-invariant positive-time algebra in the OS seminorm.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 178 identifies a sharper obstruction than previous cycles: Wilson-loop trace continuity must be checked on mixed reflected OS pairings, because \(Q(F,c)\) contains \(\Theta F_i\cdot F_j\). Even if each individual Wilson loop has a valid same-theory collar limit, the reflected product can develop a boundary cusp, hairpin, or contact renormalization at \(t=0\). Thus the real bridge lemma is not simply no-new-boundary-renormalization for single loops; it is no-new-boundary-renormalization for every finite OS matrix entry. The local mirror-flat sector remains plausibly solved by distributional continuity, so the next decisive falsifier or proof must come from mixed Wilson pairings.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Analyze the simplest mixed Wilson OS entry: take two small rectangular loops in \(t>0\), collar them by distance \(\delta\), reflect one, and compute or bound the possible boundary contact/cusp renormalization of \(S_{a,L}(\Theta W_R(C_\delta)W_R(C_\delta))\) as \(a\downarrow0\) then \(\delta\downarrow0\). The experiment should decide whether the reflected product has only the prescribed perimeter/local renormalization or an extra boundary factor.
